To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a hybrid control system can be designed to achieve a desired closed-loop performance and that this system is computationally inexpensive.

a digital control scheme can be designed for any continuous-time LTI system that is stable and can be stabilized by an LTI controller, and that the design can be done in a way that minimizes the processing time of the digital controller.

(1) a digital-control scheme is presented that can implement every stabilizing (LTL) controller for high-frequency sampling, and (2) a method is given that finds the least-precise digital controller that can implement every LTI controller satisfying a prescribed design specification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of a robust hybrid controller that can be implemented with limited computational power and operate at high frequencies.
the design of a robust hybrid controller that can implement every stabilizing continuous-time LTI controllers and operate at high sampling frequencies.
the design of robust digital controllers that can operate at high frequencies with limited computational power, thus making them suitable for real-time embedded systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the digital control of high-frequency applications with low-cost computation has been made possible by our proposed approach.
this work presents a new design methodology for digital control that is suitable for high-frequency applications.
this thesis has provided a systematic approach to the design of embedded control systems for high-frequency applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel hybrid controller that is robust against sampling and computational errors and is computationally efficient.
the proposed digital-control scheme is a practical alternative to the existing digital-control schemes for high-frequency sampled-data control systems.
we propose a novel digital-control scheme for high-frequency applications and present a method for synthesizing the corresponding digital controllers with the least computational cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a digital-control system can be designed with a high sampling frequency, which is essential for many applications, and with a small computational load, which is important for embedded control.
the design of high-speed digital-control systems can be carried out in two steps.
, in contrast to the conventional digital control, a high-frequency hybrid controller is robust to measurement and computational uncertainties.
